newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Brussels bourse stages another surprise party.
newsitem.headline: Brussels bourse stages another surprise party.

text.p: Wall Street's strong early showing coupled with solid bonds and a modest recovery of the dollar sparked another party for the Bel-20 index on Monday.
The index added 0.74 percent, or 16.39 points to 2,242.37 points with 2.03 billion francs in Belgian shares traded.
"I had expected a stronger (negative) impact of the dollar," said Wim Van Dijk at Generale Bank.
The Bel-20 was marked nearly half a percent higher before the Dow got into its stride and notched up one percent. "If Wall Street continues like this, we'll be allright," Van Dijk said.
Dealers said sellers stuck to the sidelines. "The market is almost totally empty (on the ask side)" one said.
Investors were expected to hold on further to their stock ahead of a string of U.S. economic data later this week which might offer fresh hints about the U.S. interest rate outlook.
Comments late last week by Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan had already assuaged fears over the near-term outlook for interest rates.
Oil major Petrofina, the market leader in value terms, gained a meagre 0.2 percent to 12,800 francs. But its warrant soared nine percent to 197 francs.

Traders say PetroFina is being supported ahead of the expiry of a warrant on its shares, which can be exercised between May 20 and June 3 at a ratio of one share for one warrant at a price of 12,500 francs.

Traders noted the lack of impact from comments by PetroFina's CEO Francois Cornelis, ahead of the annual shareholders meeting, that earnings nearly doubled in the first four months of 1997 and that the company wanted an annual net profit of 20 billion francs by the year 2000.
"It's clear that management is doing whatever it can to lift the share price," one trader said.
Construction company Franki, which also held its annual shareholders meeting on Monday, was the day's leading gainer with a 7.2 percent leap to 461 francs.

One trader said that reports that Franki's leading shareholders Frankipar and Group Van Roey had increased their joint stake to nearly 62 percent from 60.4 percent might be fanning investor confidence in the stock.
Holding company Gevaert was another noteable gainer with a 6.3 percent rise to 2,850 but traders were not immediately able to explain its performance.
